title: Renewable Energy Comparisons: Calculations

final_note: Renewable maths cracked. Numbers now reveal the true winners.

walkthroughs.body_html: Annual energy (MWh) = capacity (MW) x capacity factor x 8760. A 5 MW wind turbine at 40 percent capacity factor: 5 x 0.40 x 8760 = 17,520 MWh per year. A 5 MW UK solar farm at 11 percent: 5 x 0.11 x 8760 = 4818 MWh per year. The wind turbine produces nearly four times more for the same nameplate capacity.

Solar PV needs roughly 1 hectare per MW (10,000 m2). Onshore wind needs around 0.3 hectare per MW including turbine bases and access roads, but the wider site can still be used for farming or grazing. Tidal lagoons need huge coastal areas but produce predictable power. Comparing footprints helps land-use planning.

LCOE divides total lifetime cost by total lifetime energy. UK LCOE estimates (around 2024) in pounds per MWh: onshore wind 40 to 50, offshore wind 50 to 60, solar PV 35 to 50, gas 80 to 120, nuclear 100 plus. Renewable LCOE has fallen by around 80 percent over the last decade, making them cheapest new build in many markets.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Biomass”?
options: Captures kinetic and potential energy of tides; predictable but site-limited.
Uses heat from Earth's interior to generate electricity or heat buildings (e.g., Iceland).
Burning organic matter (wood, crops, waste) for energy; carbon-neutral if regrown sustainably.
Photovoltaic cells convert sunlight directly into electricity via the photoelectric effect.
